messages:
mike: FYI hitting a perf regression on Mixtral long sequences after the recent kernel-selection tweak. Tail p95 for seq_len=2048 went up ~18% on GQA configs.

mike: Traced it down to KV-cache hot paths — when paged KV fragmentation happens we seem to fall back to a slower attention kernel. Not sure if it is kernel selection logic or cache layout.

perf-bot: quick profile snapshot (pid=4521):
```
KV-cache: hits=92.1% misses=7.9% frag=1.0%
selected_kernel: attention_fused_fp16_v2 -> fallback attention_split_tf32
avg_token_latency_ms: 7.2 -> 8.5 (seq=2048, batch=1)
cpu-ms: 12.4 gpu-ms: 7.1
```

tara: @mike can you paste the model config used? GQA vs MQA layout matters a lot for num_key_value_heads/kv_dim.

mike: Config used: Mixtral-8x, GQA promoted to MQA with num_key_value_heads=64, kv_dim=128, kv_paging=enabled. Routing picks this model for long seqs.

sahil: Quick thought: setting num_key_value_heads to a power-of-two that aligns with kernel vector width (e.g., 32) usually avoids the fallback path. Also kv_dim=64 often maps to faster fused kernels on A100. If kv_dim % 64 != 0 we get slower kernels.

jen: We merged a kernel-selection heuristic change 2 commits ago that prefers "compatibility" kernels when fragmentation>0.5% — that might be the immediate cause. Reverting or tightening the threshold could help.

mike: Reproducer command I used: `REDWOOD_PROF=1 ./serve --model mixtral-8x --max-seq 2048 --batch 1 --route=gqa->mqa`

tara: Can you capture `nvprof` or `nsys` trace and the runtime selection log? Also include the kv page layout dump (we have `--dump-kv-layout` flag).

mike: Attached small dump excerpt (trimmed):
```
KV pages: total_pages=4096 allocated=3970 free_frag_pages=126
page_layout: [interleaved: 60%, tiled: 40%]
paged_fragmentation_pct=3.07
```

sahil: That fragmentation is small but enough to trigger the heuristic Jen mentioned. Two approaches: 1) change cache layout to prefer tiled layout for Mixtral when num_key_value_heads>32, or 2) force the fused attention path by aligning kv_dim/head counts. For throughput, option (2) is quickest.

sahil: Suggested quick config to test:
```
model.override.num_key_value_heads=32
model.override.kv_dim=64
runtime.kernel_selection.force_fused=true
```

tara: Also consider adjusting batching heuristics: for long seqs we currently cap batch at 4 and use max_delay_ms=5 — that amplifies per-request tail latency. Experiment with batch cap=2 / delay=2 for latency-critical routes.

jen: I'll revert the compatibility-threshold change in a canary branch and run CI perf tests. If that fixes the immediate regression we can then evaluate the longer-term layout changes.

mike: Ran sahil's quick config locally: num_key_value_heads=32, kv_dim=64 -> p95 dropped back to baseline, avg token latency 7.1ms. Throughput looks stable.

perf-bot: regression-check result:
```
branch: revert/compat-threshold-canary
metric: p95(seq2048,batch1)
baseline: 7.2ms
current: 7.0ms
delta: -2.8%
```

mike: Nice. Action items: @sahil to run wider matrix for Mixtral/Mistral/Qwen with 32/64 KV head/dim combos and record kernel selection; @jen to run canary revert and verify on staging; @tara to evaluate batching heuristic adjustments for long-seq routes.

sahil: I'll upload a small matrix CSV and a script to synthesize page layouts to reproduce fragmentation locally. Will test paged vs monolithic KV layouts too.

mike: Thanks. Also note RoPE scaling impacts: for Qwen configs we saw RoPE scale changes change attention block size and trigger kernel remap — include RoPE scaling in the matrix.

jen: Good call. I'll add RoPE_scaling as a factor in canary perf runs.

mike: tagging this thread as a chase for the perf backlog. Will follow up with results tomorrow. :eyes:
